frequency_question: How often do U.S. presidents follow through on sweeping, punitive trade tariff threats against close allies within the stated window of their announcement?
membership_rule: Includes instances where a U.S. president formally announces or threatens major broad-based tariffs against a close trading partner/ally, where execution depends primarily on executive authority (will and capability). Excludes standard statutory anti-dumping/countervailing duty processes managed by agencies unless driven directly by executive decree.

cases.name: Reagan Japanese semiconductor and electronics tariffs
Trump Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs (Canada/Mexico/EU)
Trump threatened Mexico tariff over border (escalation)

coverage_note: 5 major distinct historical instances of direct executive tariff declarations against major partners identified.
known_gaps: Some minor or fleeting threats used purely as rhetorical leverage are omitted as they never reached formal administrative scheduling.
skeleton: Executive trade threat instances categorized by unilateral authority use versus negotiation leverage usage.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 named clear executive tariff threat implementations where statutory authority was directly invoked.
validity_reason: Valid for the duration of the current presidential term structure and executive trade authorities under current statutory frameworks.
